problem_statement: SuccessfullSites/Agency-Website is a static, single-page marketing landing served directly from index.html with a local style.css and per-section component scripts under components/ that inject their markup on load (no build step). The page has already been rebranded into Groundline, a field-service scheduling and dispatch platform, and it now carries a 'Dispatch coverage' proof surface built from three shared pieces: (1) a dispatch coverage strip in the metrics section (#Metric) whose row of four count tiles (dispatch board / offline field app / multi-branch rollup / first-time-fix) summarizes coverage; (2) a shared 'Dispatch coverage' rail rendered by components/coverage-rail.js into the hero, metrics, and footer sections (section-modifier classes coverage-rail--hero / --metrics / --footer); and (3) a coverage filter control in #Metric whose buttons (All / By branch / By crew / By region) drive a #coverage-readout 'Showing: ... coverage' label wired by components/coverage-filter.js. A regression has broken this proof surface on the current build: on a 390px phone the coverage strip row is pinned to a fixed non-wrapping width so it pushes the document past the viewport (horizontal overflow); the shared coverage rail no longer renders in the metrics and footer sections; and the coverage filter click no longer re-syncs the readout, so after choosing 'By branch' the label is stuck on 'Showing: all coverage'. Repair the proof surface so it is production-grade: make the coverage strip row wrap/shrink so it never overflows the 390px viewport (keep tablet and desktop intact); restore the shared 'Dispatch coverage' rail in the hero, metrics AND footer sections; keep the rail and strip on the ivory Groundline palette so they stay visually faithful to the reference (do not recolor them into a dark slab); and wire the coverage filter so a click live-reads the chosen scope and updates #coverage-readout to 'Showing: branch coverage' (and the matching label for crew / region / all). Keep the single-page section structure, the nav anchors, the component scripts, the local image assets, and the Groundline copy across every captured section intact.
required_content: The dispatch coverage strip row in #Metric wraps or shrinks its four count tiles so a 390px phone has no horizontal overflow, while the tablet and desktop layouts stay intact.
The shared 'Dispatch coverage' rail renders in the hero, metrics AND footer sections (coverage-rail--hero, coverage-rail--metrics, coverage-rail--footer are all present).

The coverage rail and dispatch strip keep the ivory Groundline palette (light rail background, dark navy text) and stay visually faithful to the reference rather than being recolored into a dark slab.

Clicking a coverage filter button live-reads the chosen scope and updates #coverage-readout, so after choosing 'By branch' the readout reads 'Showing: branch coverage' (not the stale 'Showing: all coverage').

The Groundline field-service rebrand remains complete across the captured sections (Smart Scheduling, Crew Dispatch, Parts Inventory, Field Analytics, Customer Invoicing) with no leftover Landify demo copy.
The footer (#Footer) shows the Groundline credit with no 'SuccessfullSite' template-author credit.
design_constraints: Repair only the coverage proof surface: the dispatch strip row layout (style.css), the shared rail presence (components/coverage-rail.js), the rail/strip palette (style.css), and the filter readout wiring (components/coverage-filter.js). Keep the single-page shell, nav anchors, component mount points, and the Groundline copy untouched.
Keep the coverage rail and dispatch strip on the ivory Groundline palette faithful to the reference; do not restyle them into a dark theme or otherwise diverge visually from the design anchors.

The coverage strip row must reflow (wrap or shrink its tiles) at 390px with no horizontal overflow beyond 24px; do not fake the fix by clipping overflow on an inner element while the row stays fixed-width.
Keep the site fully static and served from index.html with zero remote requests on render; Bootstrap CSS, Bootstrap Icons, and Bootstrap JS are vendored locally.
Preserve the single-page section structure and responsive behavior across the hero, features, metrics, pricing, and FAQ sections.
state_constraints: The home states (desktop, mobile, tablet) capture the scrolled-to-top hero; the Groundline brand and hero headline must land above the fold on desktop_home.

The section states scroll to their anchors: desktop_features and mobile_features to #Features, desktop_metrics and mobile_metrics to #Metric, desktop_pricing to #Pricing, desktop_faq to #FAQ, and desktop_footer to #Footer, so the coverage strip, rail, and filter are captured in place.
desktop_coverage_filter scrolls to #Metric and clicks the 'By branch' coverage filter button; the post-click #coverage-readout must read 'Showing: branch coverage'.

change_completion: The dispatch coverage strip row renders its four count tiles within the 390px viewport with no horizontal overflow.
The shared 'Dispatch coverage' rail appears in the hero, metrics, and footer sections.
A coverage filter click updates the #coverage-readout terminal label to the selected scope ('Showing: branch coverage' after choosing 'By branch').
design_consistency: The Groundline ivory palette, rail chrome, dispatch-strip tile styling, and brand accent are preserved.
The coverage rail and strip keep the ivory/navy editorial look and stay visually faithful to the reference across the metrics and footer sections rather than diverging into a dark slab.
interaction_continuity: Clicking a coverage filter button updates the 'Showing:' readout to the selected scope (the post-click terminal state reflects the choice, not the default 'all coverage').
regression: The Groundline nav brand, hero, features grid, metrics band, pricing tiers, FAQ, and footer remain reachable and unchanged in copy.
The static site serves from index.html with a clean browser console (zero disallowed errors).
responsive: 390px home, features, and metrics plus the 834px tablet home have no horizontal overflow beyond 24px.
The coverage strip tiles wrap or shrink cleanly instead of forcing a fixed-width row.

author_notes: Repo-grounded static single-page L4 REGRESSION-CONTINUITY REPAIR. The Groundline rebrand is the shared substrate (identical across all three legs); the graded work is repairing the 'Dispatch coverage' proof surface, which fails on four ORTHOGONAL gates in the broken build. D6 no_horizontal_overflow: the dispatch-strip row is pinned to a fixed non-wrapping width and overflows the 390px viewport. D3 visual_regression: the coverage rail/strip must stay on the ivory Groundline palette faithful to the reference (the bad negative control recolors them into a dark navy slab; the baseline is missing the rails). D2 dom_assertions: the shared coverage rail must render in the hero, metrics AND footer sections (section-modifier classes coverage-rail--metrics / --footer); baseline drops all rails, bad keeps only the hero rail. D4 interaction_assertions: the coverage filter click must live-read the chosen scope and update #coverage-readout; the bad control's stale-closure handler toggles .active (the interaction trajectory succeeds) but leaves the readout on 'Showing: all coverage' so the terminal state is dead. The only leg-varying files are style.css, components/coverage-rail.js, and components/coverage-filter.js. A console-clean measurement-enabling infrastructure change (.app{overflow-x:visible} plus pinning the off-screen offcanvas drawer and hero decorative bands, and vendoring Bootstrap locally) is applied identically to all three legs so the overflow gate measures only the graded strip and the runtime-health gate reflects the repair, not template scenery or removed CDN requests.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: Static single-page Groundline (SuccessfullSites Agency-Website) marketing landing whose per-section component scripts host a shared 'Dispatch coverage' proof surface (strip + rail + filter). It is an ideal host for an L4 regression_continuity repair whose four graded gates are orthogonal: mobile overflow of the strip row, cross-section presence of the shared rail, visual fidelity of the rail/strip palette, and the post-click terminal state of the filter readout.
